I was shocked by my visit to dentist Nina Lionidovna Ovchinnikova. I've been to the clinic on Korzhovka many times, using free numbing as a multi-child mother to save on budget. The numbing had never failed me before, so I saw no point in paying extra. Now, I came to see Ovchinnikova with pain in my left lower 5th tooth, planning to fix the 7th one later. She started raising her voice at me, saying the 5th tooth was perfectly healthy and didn't need treatment, that she's been working for a long time and knows better than me. Meanwhile, she was poking at the 7th tooth, causing me pain, and asked if she should continue. I didn't argue, let her start with the 7th. Last time, they'd diagnosed a cavity in the 5th tooth, and it was hurting, but now it was supposedly healthy? She gave me a shot, waited, then started drilling. The pain was sharp and intense, the numbing didn't work at all. She raised her voice at me, saying it shouldn't hurt and I was an unreasonable patient. When I asked why she was being rude, she said I was the rude one. After another shot, the numbing finally worked. But Ovchinnikova said it couldn't have worked that fast. I must be faking it for fun. They cleaned the canals for a long time, doing an X-ray twice because they didn't clean it properly the first time. In the end, she told me the tooth couldn't be further treated and the pain would last from two days to two weeks. They made me sign something in my chart, and I was free to go. I don't know what I signed. I was on the verge of fainting. With such attitude, one shouldn't work with people. I also wondered if she deliberately harmed me, so the tooth would need to be removed later. Why should the pain last for two weeks if the nerve was removed?

I arrived by prior appointment with two small children: a 5-year-old boy and a 2.5-year-old girl. We needed to have photopломбы placed. We were scheduled for 13:00 and 14:00. Arriving at the clinic at 12:45, we were directed to the registration desk to fill out forms. The woman at the registration desk had a very important air about her and handed me two contracts, saying, "Fill these out." I learned from her that getting a card costs 600 rubles. I objected, saying that if it's paid, maybe she could fill it out herself, as I would dictate the information. She refused, saying she had more important work to do, although there was no one else around the registration desk. Previously, when my son's teeth were treated in other clinics, they never asked me to fill out anything, they did it all themselves quickly and efficiently, and I just signed and paid. Naturally, I refused to fill it out myself and called the specialist we were scheduled to see. It was already 13:00. The specialist, a woman with a pleasant voice, heard about my problem and said she would come down and sort it out. A minute later, I saw her, and she explained that I needed to pay 1200 rubles for the first consultation, not for the card. I replied that we didn't need a consultation, I had no objection to the card, but we just needed to have photopломбы placed. In response, she sternly declared that if I didn't want to consult and get a card, she couldn't take us, adding that it was our problem. In the end, she said, "Sort out your own problems" and left.
I thought that if we were scheduled with her at 13:00 and 14:00 and she treated us like this, there were probably another 20-25 people without an appointment waiting for her, so she didn't value her clients much.
After all this, I went home. Fortunately, there's another good clinic where the children have an appointment scheduled for the day after this one.

Today, April 6, 2015, at 14:00, my son German (born in 1999) went to Polyclinic No. 128 to see pediatrician Kuznetsova (during her office hours) to get a referral. At the registration desk, where he went to get a ticket, he was immediately redirected to the adolescent clinic, which was closed at that time. Son could not get the referral on the appointed day by the doctor and returned home empty-handed.
The same situation happened in February of this year on February 16. I went to the registration desk at 16:00 to get my son's card. The lady sitting in front of the window didn't even bother to look for the card on the shelves, she immediately sent me to the adolescent clinic, which was already closed at that time. But I am an adult and at my request the clinic was opened. The card was not there. The girls from the adolescent clinic went out of their way and made a temporary card. In the end, we managed to see the specialist.
Now I have a question. Do I have to constantly leave work to accompany my son to the doctors because of the registration desk's work? I am not on a salary, no one pays for my lost time.
Is it really impossible to check their shelves and find the card??? Or is it not part of their duties? Of course, it's easier to automatically send to the "garden" upon hearing the year of birth and not get up from your seat. Let the patients run around the offices with their tongues out and come to get the referral for several days in a row.

I'm utterly shocked by today's visit to the pediatrician, Sokolova (our regular pediatrician is on vacation, she's substituting). She was rude to me from the moment I stepped in, even before I entered the office. "Who are you?" she asked, "And where's your card?" It's a strange question since this wonderful clinic doesn't give out cards. She sat there staring at her computer for 10 minutes, I was waiting, my grandmother went to the registrar to find out about the card's fate. Then they brought the card and the doctor deigned to ask why we were there. After hearing that another pediatrician heard heart murmurs in the child, she asked a brilliant question: "So, what do you want me to do, listen to it?" I replied that it would be nice. She didn't listen, just gave a referral to the cardiologist (forgetting to mention that he won't be there for 1.5 months). Her tone and manner of speaking scared the child (she was rude, to put it mildly). Looking at the child, who was about to cry, she said, "Well, do something, you're raising him." I wanted to ask what she's doing there, getting a salary from the money that people pay in taxes. And another question to the administration: why hasn't the issue of how cards get to the doctors been resolved for at least 1.5 years? If you don't give out cards, create a system that works and not every second person who comes in has to run between the office and the registrar looking for their card.

A heavy-duty hospital patient needed a medication that couldn't be bought anywhere in St. Petersburg on Friday. The price was 28,000 rubles and above. It was ordered through wer.ru. Delivery was from Moscow on Tuesday. Until Tuesday, 9 tablets were borrowed from another patient with a promise to return them on Tuesday morning. Also, a car was ordered for Tuesday morning to transport the patient for treatment 250 km away from St. Petersburg.
To cut the story short, the medication wasn't delivered.
It started with a call from the courier around noon, who indifferently informed us that our medication had been delivered to another city resident by mistake, the package was opened, she was too far away and had no time, and it wasn't her responsibility anyway. Then the pharmacy called, unable to understand that they were talking about the health and treatment of a heavy-duty patient, that the medication was vital, and asked us to wait until tomorrow. What "tomorrow" are they talking about when the medication needs to be taken "yesterday"?! They said the courier was on the other end of the city (this was still before lunch!), couldn't come to us, and suggested I leave my work and patients and go myself to meet the courier on the other end of the city.
You know, I've never encountered such irresponsible, indifferent attitude towards people - whether it's the courier service or the pharmacy itself, I don't care. I care about the patient's health and treatment.
Many hours were spent on phone calls - to no avail.
In the end, we had to turn to the internet again and look for the medication from other suppliers. We succeeded! And we were helped by very responsible employees of another pharmacy on Borovaya - the pharmacy manager himself delivered the medication to the patient that same day. Big thanks to them!
But I wouldn't recommend using wer.ru again - they'll let you down! There are many similar negative reviews.

We ended up at this clinic with our son last year (2014). The money-making scheme started even over the phone when making an appointment: I asked to schedule an appointment with a pediatric dentist, and since the earliest available slot was two weeks away, the girl on the phone suggested scheduling with a hygienist, saying that she also performs treatments. I was skeptical, but we scheduled an appointment anyway as we needed to address the tooth issue urgently.
On the appointed day, the doctor herself said that she doesn't handle treatments and that I must have misunderstood the receptionist. Nevertheless, she agreed to examine and clean the teeth. The hygienist (whose name I don't remember, but her first name was Ella) left a positive impression, despite a few attempts to overcharge us.
While our child was in the chair, the future dentist, Matveeva E., entered the room. The hygienist praised our child's behavior, but Matveeva seemed disinterested, with a blank stare and the thought "how annoying you all are" written on her forehead. I attributed this to her being busy with another patient. However, when we went for our appointment with Matveeva, the same thing happened. She treated our child like a non-entity and answered my questions condescendingly, as if she had just transferred from a public clinic to a private one and hadn't adjusted yet. In the end, we decided not to have her treat our child's teeth. To top it off, we heard a male doctor in the neighboring room raising his voice and a child crying (the child was alone in the room). After that, we vowed never to return to Zubrenka.
And yes, for such high fees, we could get better service at the local clinic, where they would lick our hands and shower our child with care and attention. In the end, we returned to the local clinic for our dental needs.

aspect_term: neurologists L.L. Goloborodko and O.R. Kuznetsova
english_translated:
I want to leave a negative review about the neurologists L.L. Goloborodko and O.R. Kuznetsova.

Their negligence and indifference almost led to serious health problems for me.
I'll start by saying that in March 2013, I went to Goloborodko L.L. with severe back pain. The doctor examined me, administered a block, injected painkillers, ordered an X-ray, and prescribed: milgamma, dip rylif, painkillers, etc. After that, thankfully, my back pain subsided, and I started swimming and doing special exercises. However, in September 2014 (after 1.5 years), I again went to Goloborodko with severe back pain. The doctor followed the same scheme, adding physiotherapy and ksefokam injections, which I faithfully attended, but they were ineffective.

The next time, I decided not to go to L.L. but to make an appointment with O.R. Kuznetsov (who was highly praised). Yes, the doctor conducted a more thorough examination of my spine (also looked at the X-ray results), and said: you have a very strong spinal curvature. I'm canceling the physiotherapy, canceling the ksefokam prescribed by Goloborodko, as it's ineffective in your case. Swimming also turns out to be harmful, according to him (despite the fact that swimming is generally recommended for spinal problems). Meanwhile, I paid more than 1000 rubles for the ksefokam prescribed by L.L.

It's great: one doctor experiments and prescribes, the other experiments and cancels, and the patient suffers both physically and financially!

Moreover, when I went to O.R. Kuznetsov, I said that I hadn't found any relief from L.L.'s treatment: my back continued to hurt despite the medication, injections, physiotherapy, etc. And I'm only 30! Neither of the mentioned doctors thought to prescribe an MRI!

Of course, I went to another clinic, where they immediately prescribed an MRI, which was approved by my insurance without any questions. The MRI showed multiple Schmorl's nodes in the thoracic spine. And I was prescribed a completely different, appropriate treatment, which actually helped me feel better.

After visiting these "doctors," I don't want to go to this clinic again, despite believing that there are also good doctors there.

The doctor examined me, administered a block, injected painkillers, ordered an X-ray, and prescribed: milgamma, dip rylif, painkillers, etc. After that, thankfully, my back pain subsided, and I started swimming and doing special exercises. The next time, I decided not to go to L.L. but to make an appointment with O.R. Kuznetsov (who was highly praised). Yes, the doctor conducted a more thorough examination of my spine (also looked at the X-ray results), and said: you have a very strong spinal curvature. I'm canceling the physiotherapy, canceling the ksefokam prescribed by Goloborodko, as it's ineffective in your case. Swimming also turns out to be harmful, according to him (despite the fact that swimming is generally recommended for spinal problems). Meanwhile, I paid more than 1000 rubles for the ksefokam prescribed by L.L.

It's great: one doctor experiments and prescribes, the other experiments and cancels, and the patient suffers both physically and financially!

And I was prescribed a completely different, appropriate treatment, which actually helped me feel better.

After visiting these "doctors," I don't want to go to this clinic again, despite believing that there are also good doctors there.

On 06.10.2015, I visited the FGBU Polyklinika No.1 of the Russian Academy of Sciences (101000, Moscow, Sretenka Boulevard, 6/1, Sretenka Boulevard metro station) to see an ENT doctor, whose exact name I don't know (possibly Simkina Natalia Valentinovna), who was taking patients in room 307.

Firstly, not only is there no electronic queue, but there's also no possibility to schedule appointments. It's just a live queue with elderly people and the ensuing consequences: "I was here first", "I've already been here", "I just want to ask".

When I went to room 307, there was only one patient being seen, and no one else was waiting for an appointment in that room. I ended up waiting by the door for more than an hour. After examining my left ear, the doctor said it was clean and there were no foreign bodies. The examination took only 3 minutes.

When I asked for a more thorough examination, I was met with rudeness from this doctor. After taking my chart, I went to the registration desk and demanded the complaint book. The staff tried to resolve the issue and sent me to the 5th floor to see the hospital director, but he wasn't there.

Upon returning, I insisted on getting the complaint book, but they said they didn't know where it was because this situation was unprecedented. They promised to look into it.

Meanwhile, at the registration desk, they sent me to see another ENT doctor, Oleynik Pavel Anatolyevich, in room 309 without waiting in line. After listening to his disapproving comments about my behavior, he examined me.

His conclusion was similar: the eardrum was clean. There was a 3 mm traumatic erosion on the lower wall of the left external auditory canal. That's all!

Today, 07.10.2015, I went to another clinic. The ENT doctor there found a foreign body (a hair) in my left ear, removed it, and cleaned the ear. I'm very grateful to her.

My conclusion: the ENT staff there is incompetent and rude. I'll never go back there, even if they introduce electronic queues or scheduling.

On October 26, 2013, I checked my vision with Dr. Kapunova and bought glasses at the "Linsmaster" salon located in the "Our" shopping center (Solntsevo). I bought glasses for distance vision, with a 2-week warranty. I've been wearing glasses since 2000. On October 22, 2013, I checked my vision at the city clinic (-2 and -1.5), and they gave me a prescription for -1.5 and -1.25. Before buying glasses, I decided to make sure I had the correct prescription from our district doctors and went to the salon for a vision check and further purchase, which is located in my district. The vision check was quite quick (-2 and -1.5), which surprised me, as I didn't receive any advice on the correct frame or lens selection. I ignored the difference from the clinic's prescription, as I believed that large networks of famous brands employ highly qualified specialists, and the diagnosis at Linsmaster costs 500 rubles. They wrote a prescription for -1.5 and -1.0. They started offering anti-scratch lenses, as they didn't have regular ones, and I would have to wait a long time (I didn't ask how long). They quickly offered anti-scratch lenses for an additional 1100 rubles, which I agreed to, as the price was reasonable considering my inexpensive frame. The glasses cost 2999 rubles. After wearing them for a week (from October 26 to November 2), my right eye (dominant) was watery, I had headaches, and I felt discomfort. I doubted the correctness of the lens selection and vision check. On November 2, 2013, I went to a familiar person (whom I found only on October 31) to check my vision again, for the third time, to see if it was correct or not. They checked my vision and gave me a prescription for -1.5 and -1.25. When I returned to this salon, they refunded everything according to the warranty, but they spoke a lot about how this couldn't happen, that I wasn't used to wearing glasses (I guess I should get used to them over years, losing even more vision from such diagnosis). They only refunded the money for the frame and lenses, and they don't have a program for incorrect diagnosis, as the employee of Linsmaster told me. After this experience, I was very happy to have a familiar person who can correctly diagnose vision and select lenses. This is my story related to Linsmaster. Please consider it and make your conclusions.

I won't go into other details of our brief communication. Why have a schedule if she can just take another patient without calling, warning, or asking if I would even come or the reason for my delay? Not to mention that my entire further schedule was disrupted (everyone is busy, and it's important to value everyone's time). When Petreykov learned that the head of the gynecological department of this hospital was a friend of my husband's family, he began to doubt his diagnosis, repeatedly saying he might be wrong, but it rarely happens as he is a category one doctor, and then he started talking about his work in Israel.
What I was going through at that moment is indescribable. I sat there crying, waiting for my husband to arrive, while Petreykov walked around me, expressing concern that I was crying, asking if I was offended by his diagnosis, and saying I should come back in 3 months to try again. Fortunately, the ambulance arrived and took me to the hospital. In the 6th gynecological department of the 23rd hospital, wonderful doctors Pazychov A. A. andFadeev I. E. examined me and said there were no signs of an ectopic pregnancy, the ultrasound also showed everything was normal, and there was no large amount of blood in the abdomen (in fact, at a 10-day delay, an ectopic pregnancy shows no symptoms and cannot be detected). Nevertheless, I was hospitalized and had daily tests. On the evening of the 27th, I started having bloody discharge, and the doctors said I had a missed abortion at an early stage. No surgery was needed, it would pass on its own. On the 30th, after a few days of observation and with good test results, I was discharged.
I want to warn everyone not to go to Petreykov. After what happened to me, I read many negative reviews about this doctor. He gives false diagnoses, his main goal is to make as much money as possible, he doesn't care about anyone's health or tears. He can put someone on the operating table for his own benefit, without considering the consequences. When he looks at a person, he sees only zeros that can go into his pocket.

I have a small, still inoperable hernia in the lumbar spine and several protrusions. After giving birth, it got much worse: the pain radiated to my leg, and I couldn't put weight on it. I hesitated for a long time before going to Bубновский, but two of my close acquaintances were very satisfied with his treatment. To be on the safe side, I first consulted with my local neurologist and then at the Institute of Neurology of the Russian Academy of Medical Sciences to have at least a couple more opinions and something to compare it with.
Having read many negative reviews online, I was prepared for the worst. However, the first consultation went well, the LFK doctor told me about my problem roughly the same as the other two doctors. She explained in detail what I needed to do, how, and why, and how long it would take to see results. She said I needed to learn to do all the exercises correctly myself, and after three treatment cycles, I should go to an ordinary gym and continue exercising on my own. She didn't put any pressure on me and didn't mention the sauna, which was complained about so much in the reviews. I don't even want to mention the complaints about the changing room: it seems like people go there not to be treated, but to spend pleasant hours in the changing room.
I started exercising on the machines, attending gymnastics, and having regular check-ups with the doctor. For a long time, I didn't feel any improvement, but I didn't get worse either. Around the 12th-15th session, there was a slight worsening, after which I felt better and the pain went away quite suddenly and noticeably. I completed two cycles and didn't go for the third because it's still very expensive; however, the pain went away.
Now I go to an ordinary gym to maintain my form and do the same exercises and attend similar gymnastics.
In fact, with such a not-so-scary problem as mine, I could have gone to an ordinary gym right away, and they would have helped me just as well, because all these elements of therapeutic physical culture are well-known and not new. But it was a bit scary: it's better to be safe with your back. Overall, I don't regret going to Bубновский and learned a bit about feeling my body and the basic exercises.
As for the negative reviews, I think people just don't know what they expect from this center: it's not a classic clinic, so why should there be any neuroхирурги working there? No one promises that. They warn about crises and increased pain. They teach how to use the machines correctly and not to take more weight than allowed, etc. And in the end, we sign a contract, so we should learn to read what we sign!
I think patients with back problems should understand that nothing can be done through pain, and they should take care of themselves. Of course, neither doctors nor instructors will force you to do something if it's painful, heavy, or uncomfortable; you just need to say if something isn't right.
And yes, they can't help everyone and not with every problem. They openly say this and send people for classic treatment, not inviting them in (I know a personal example of this too).
Overall, I'm satisfied with the treatment, the only downside is the huge price: it's just overpayment for the brand.

Good evening! I want to address, first and foremost, the dear women, although men could also benefit from this review. Dear ones, I want to warn you about this ominous place. The "doctors'" qualifications and diplomas bought in the metro underpass maim lives and shatter destinies. I was examined twice at Nataly-Med. The first time, they insisted I terminate my pregnancy due to alleged deviations (I regret now that I listened to these ignoramuses and made a mistake; I understand now that there were no grounds for an abortion). The second time, while pregnant, I went to submit samples and have an ultrasound. At an incredibly early stage, they detected a non-developing pregnancy, but the heartbeat was audible. How can there be a heartbeat at such an early stage (4 weeks) - this is clear medical stupidity. After that, I went to a genuinely qualified medical institution, where thank God everything was fine, and it turned out that the ultrasound image from Nataly-Med did not belong to me (in other words, it was someone else's random image). And the constant recommendations to "terminate the pregnancy", "you need to have an abortion", "you need to urgently terminate the pregnancy" - it seems like they have some kind of quota to fill, or some material to hand over, like traffic police officers. In any case, everyone decides for themselves where, how, and with whom to be examined, who to trust with their health. But I urge, dear women - this is not the place to trust. I repeat - do not ruin your lives, your loved ones', your children's lives. I regret endlessly that I listened to them, went along with them, and made the biggest mistake of my life. Everyone, be healthy!

I want to give my assessment of the Clinic on Leninsky Prospekt and about the surgeon, Klimenko Konstantin Vladimirovich. Perhaps this will help those who are thinking about where to go and where it is better to have an operation. I stumbled upon this clinic on the internet and immediately got the impression that everything is fast, high-quality, and beautiful. Thinking this way, I made an appointment and ended up with this surgeon. During the appointment, he looked at me and said that after the operation, I could go home immediately and full healing would take 20-25 days. When I told him that the recovery periods of others are significantly longer and that not everyone stitches the wound completely, but looks at the resected area, I heard the answer that they are all incompetent (idiots) and don't understand anything about this. This should have probably raised an alarm, but I really wanted to get rid of this problem as soon as possible and scheduled the operation. I came at the appointed time and it turned out that another operation was scheduled for my time, although I think that by paying a considerable amount of money, you should get appropriate treatment. Moreover, they took a young man who came to them in the morning, they fed him with promises all morning that he would lie down soon, but he only lay down at the appointed time for me at 18:00. I had to wait in the ward for an additional two hours. During the operation, I asked again about the rehabilitation period. And a miracle happened! It turned out that the period had increased from 20 days to 2 months, and maybe more. It won't be possible to leave after the operation immediately, as written on the website, but you need to wait for 2-3 hours for the anesthesia to wear off. And forget about sitting in a car and driving. They let me go and said to come back in 3 days for a bandage change. At first, they called me and asked about my well-being and even came home once. But this was only until I paid the remaining amount. In fact, the amount written in the contract was less, the remaining amount the doctor took for himself. In principle, I don't mind this approach, if not for the attitude. After that, they simply forgot about me and no longer asked about the healing process. If I hadn't gone to the bandage change with Golovko Yevgeny Borisovich, I don't know how the healing would have gone. Because he found stitches that my surgeons didn't see, and we tried various ointments to speed up the processes. The operation was performed on March 7, and the full healing of the wound occurred on June 10. I want to say to everyone who is thinking about an operation with Klimenko, think and look for other surgeons. There are many of them, and this one should be avoided.

I've been there several times to different specialists because it's near my house. You can draw your own conclusions.
I was at dentist Kosminцева's once, I don't know what kind of specialist she is, but she put a filling of a different color than my tooth, showed it in the mirror and asked: "Well, how's that?" I immediately said that wouldn't do, she first started saying she would still change the color, but she did redo it.
I also went to ENT Gabedava, she treated my vasomotor rhinitis, for some reason she sent me to get an X-ray (when I got the X-ray they were very surprised why I was getting it), luckily the medication helped, but she still advised me to come back to show her how I was doing, without saying that they would charge me again for the follow-up appointment! Of course I didn't go to her. My ears were also bothering me, but she couldn't say anything except: "Come back when they're really bothering you".
In the fall, I decided to remove a bleeding mole. I went to dermatologist Marina Anatolevna (I didn't remember her last name, and it's not on the website), she smelled strongly of cigarettes. She sent me to find an oncologist because they don't have one there. She didn't tell me anything about the removal methods, just mentioned a price of 3,000 rubles, but didn't say what was included. After getting the oncologist's diagnosis from another clinic, I called ABS to find out the exact price, of course they didn't tell me anything clearly (they mentioned some unclear price of 2,000 rubles and that they have laser removal, which I was happy about). But when I came for the removal, they told me they can only remove it with electrocoagulation and there's no laser there at all. And when it came to the price, they calculated 5,700 rubles. I wanted to go to another clinic, but when I called they said I would have to pay for the dermatologist's appointment. So I had it done at ABS.
In general, I think you can go there if you need to do something specific and urgent, like an ultrasound, and the exact price is on the website. Just be prepared that the price can increase by 2 times for various reasons.
By the way, I noticed that after my visits, they started calling me from some cosmetic centers and offering free consultations, but there are many negative reviews about these centers on the internet, so I just hang up.

We first visited the clinic on 12.04.15 with an urgent complaint about a 3-year-old girl. After explaining the reason for our visit to Dr. Palladyeva, we received a couple of vague questions, and then we were invited for an examination. During the examination, the doctor immediately suggested using a hormonal ointment. Despite my explanation that we had already tried this medication without success, I received no response other than confused comments like "all doctors prescribe this." The medication was not related to the reason for our visit. The doctor then looked at me and asked if we would be getting tests done, without providing any suggestions about the current situation. She offered no comments on whether the tests were necessary or not. After that, we returned to the waiting room, where the doctor advised us to wash the girl with chamomile until the test results were ready, which would take another 3 days (despite the fact that we had come in with urgent inflammatory discharge). She said she couldn't do anything else to help. When I asked about alternative options, she didn't respond, and when I asked how to find out the test results, she directed me to the registration desk. In the end, we paid 1,700 rubles for the doctor's advice to use chamomile and wait for her equally qualified opinion (which we probably paid another 1,700 rubles for). I never write reviews, but in this case, the doctor's complete lack of knowledge and apathy is truly shocking. Please, hire at least pediatricians of a decent level.

I would like to pay tribute to all the employees of the Family Health Clinic from girls in the registry to doctors. My child got something in the eye, in the city did not know where to turn, in the waiting room just "sent", the time was about 21 pm. Called the clinic and there was no doctor at the moment, but I was not left in trouble, immediately called the doctor, the doctor came, examined the baby treatment.

We ended up there. In short, I'll start from the beginning, or rather, from the threshold. We came to inquire about which specialist to go to - my husband's back (lumbar region) hurts (prices vary for everyone, I can't remember exactly, but roughly - neurologist 900, manual therapist 1500, osteopath 3500). The administrator (probably the main one who scams) told us, you can go first to the neurologist, find out which specialist you need, but you'll pay like this - 900 + 1500 (if a consultation is needed) + 3500, so we decided, since the osteopath is also a neurologist, we'll go straight to him (appointment 3500).

Our mistake was that we didn't get an MRI done beforehand, but we asked the administrator and the doctor, do you accept without a scan? And still, maybe it's better for us to get a tomography done first and then come back to you? To which the administrator said - the doctor will tell you, and the doctor just said - we'll see (you know, you've got to make some money 3500 for the appointment).

They led my husband behind a screen (of course, for such a price that the osteopath charges, you could make a nicer cabinet and interior!), and in one cabin, several people are taken at once, someone is getting a massage, someone is with the manual therapist (it reminds me of a Soviet-era physical therapy clinic), well, the doctor twisted my husband this way and that, and then said, you had an injury at 10 (my husband is 30), you fell hard on your butt and your coccyx got dislocated and the tissues got twisted, that's why it hurts now. Well, I already found it funny, honestly, how he could determine an injury from 10 years ago. My husband couldn't remember any serious injuries, he asked his mom, she also said there were no serious injuries. Well, he fell like all children do and that's it.

IN SHORT, then he supposedly (!) put the coccyx back in place and removed the pain (but the pain didn't go away).

Saying that the pain didn't go away and it didn't even get a little better, he said, you still need to get it adjusted, come back next time. My husband came back. Another 3500 rubles, he adjusted it again. Well, it didn't get any better after the appointment (why, I wonder, and for what they took the money), in the end, the osteopath says - then I don't know what's wrong with you. You need to get a tomography done and come back to us!

After that, we didn't really want to go back.

We got a tomography done, it turned out to be herniated discs and spinal canal stenosis. I wanted to go demand my money back, but there's no one to leave the child with, but we won't be going back there.

I want to share my story with you. My dad was sent to this research institute with joint problems. The referral was given by the local clinic. After calling the registration desk, I found out that they don't accept such referrals anymore, only through the Ministry of Health, and that the referral is only for a consultation. So, I went to the Ministry of Health, waited for 3 hours, and finally got the desired referral (thank you very much for the promptness). Full of hope that my dad's suffering would finally end and he would be cured, I called the registration desk of the Institute of Rheumatology, and received a wonderful response: they only accept Ministry of Health referrals for hospitalization, and consultations are paid (pay attention to the full name of this institution: Federal State Budgetary Institution "Scientific Research Institute of Rheumatology" of the Russian Academy of Medical Sciences). Further, in confusion, I asked how this could be, since the registration desk had said just a week ago that consultations were also through the Ministry of Health, and I was told: you were simply told incorrectly. I asked for the chief doctor's phone number, they directed me to the information desk (before calling the registration desk, I tried to call the information desk for 30 minutes, but it was either busy or they didn't pick up). I tried to explain to the registrar that the information desk wasn't answering. I asked again for the chief doctor's phone number, they refused. I asked for her surname, she hung up, and for the next 15 minutes (I didn't call again after that), they didn't pick up. I can't say anything about the doctors yet, as we haven't had an appointment yet, but I want to say one thing: before taking any action, it's better to call not the registrars, but the chief doctor who signed their orders when they were hired. Because they won't just not help, they'll also misinform you. It's good that there's someone to go for dad, but imagine how many elderly people come on their own with crutches and end up with nothing because of such employees who work in this registration desk.

english_translated: I will leave a review about the gynecological department and ultrasound specialists of this so-called "medcenter". Doctor Nabatova N.I. - an ultrasound specialist - a gynecologist, in my opinion, does not even have the appropriate education, not to mention ultrasound certificates! She examined my baby during a screening for only five minutes and read all the indicators from a cheat sheet, which were then written in the results of the baby's first trimester examination. She did not write anything else, not even the nasal bone, although it was also necessary for blood analysis (blood was taken there, and they then send the analyzes to the Dialab laboratory). In addition, there is a nurse who behaves like a "barrel" and is rude as if I am in the worst clinic with an angry staff. Even when I needed to be weighed, I was asked to say my exact weight myself! Also, according to the price list, the ultrasound before 12 weeks costs 800 rubles, as I found out later, but they charged me 1000 rubles as if it were after 12 weeks, although I was 11 weeks pregnant. After complaining to the chief doctor about what was happening, I heard clumsy lies (I won't go into details) when she said one thing, then another, then a third, and after each "cornering", she continued to lie. First, she said that they do not measure the bone, then that it is not necessary for blood analysis, although it is indicated in the blood analysis, then that it is measured in the expanded ultrasound, but they do not do it there and you need to go to another center. After a week, it turned out that I needed to ask what kind of ultrasound I needed, and they cost differently there. Although when I applied to the center, no one offered a choice, and after these stories, I called again to make an appointment and they answered in surprise that they have only one type of ultrasound and no more advanced or less powerful equipment, as the chief doctor said, that they have only one! And in the end, she started shouting at me and accused me of behaving badly during the appointment, that there is a recording in the cabinets and she did not hear the nurse's rudeness! When I contacted the medical center's security service, they were also surprised and said that there is no recording. Even the video in the corridors does not always work. I intend to go to court.

I had vertebroplasty (filling with special cement) done on two of them in December 2014 at MONIKI, and I had to wait for hospitalization to strengthen the next two. The wait was very long, leading to almost complete destruction of one of the vertebrae and severe pain. Even strong painkillers didn't help. In June, I learned that the Medical Center on Dzerzhinsky Street had purchased the necessary equipment for such operations, and I turned to S.S. I am a rare but regular client of Telo's beauty clinic. I will write honestly. This clinic is like other companies, a commercial organization aimed at making a profit. It provides services in exchange for money. I will approach its description as a consumer of its services, without any special medical education. Why do I actively emphasize that it is a commercial organization? Because I want everyone who reads my review to be sure that I value my money just as much as anyone else and I don't like to part with it easily, especially not for nothing. I am fully aware of the clinic's goals and my needs. My main needs lately have been help in reducing body volume, body and face care (hydration, facial cleansing, peels, wraps, mesotherapy), hair removal, and currently hair care. At Telo's beauty clinic, they have performed: a body tite operation (thighs), hydromassage, microcurrents on the face, and wraps. This is my fourth clinic. My acquaintance with the clinic began about two years ago, initially online (on the internet). I was looking for something to help me correct my figure (specifically, to reduce the volume of my thighs, those "love handles" and if possible, the inner part of the thighs). First, I decided on the procedure that suited my needs - body tite. Then, I made a list of clinics and chose two. But I only went to Telo's Beauty because I was satisfied with their approach to working with clients, including me, and other parameters. Firstly, the clinic is not located at the other end of Moscow, secondly, the administrators are reasonable and polite. Sometimes, they may make mistakes, but it's usually minor and can be overlooked with a smile. Thirdly, of course, the doctors. My first doctor was Gulmira Shamanaeva (I don't remember her middle name). I will deviate from the chronological order to describe my meeting with Gulmira Shamanaeva and the results of my operation. She clearly explained the procedure, and I told her about the problems I wanted to solve (thigh volume and "love handles", among other things). She honestly said that the procedure would not help me become thin, but it could make some corrections. We discussed everything, decided on the list of analyzes and the time of the operation, and what I needed to buy compression underwear. The hour of truth arrived, and I came already under valerian, because I was scared. They gave me more sedatives, prepared me for the operation, which is actually done under local anesthesia. The operation lasted 3 hours, there were many anesthesia injections, it was painful, but bearable. The doctor and the nurse constantly talked to me and distracted me from the unpleasant sensations. I can't describe the operation in more detail because enough time has passed, but I can say that it was more scary than painful. It was painful later. After the operation, they helped me put on compression underwear and I left in a taxi. I went straight to sleep. But when I woke up, I couldn't raise my hands to even take a pill. I was scared, but I'm strong, so after panicking for 10 minutes, I decided to sleep more. When I woke up in the morning, I felt like I had been beaten up the day before and everything hurt. The next two days were the hardest. But I got up, went to the bathroom, got water, etc. I sent my family away, but if you're planning to do this procedure, ask someone from your family or a friend to support you, at least for the first 2-3 days. Then everything got better, the swelling went down slowly but surely, the bruises changed color and went away. On the 5th or 6th day, I started going to hydromassage (it's on the border of sadomasochism, but it helps afterwards). By the way, since I'm writing a review, I want to express my gratitude to all the specialists who do hydromassage, they supported me and helped me. Warm attitude really helps. But to avoid sounding too positive, I'll add my "but". I didn't expect that the rehabilitation after the operation would cost me so much. And this is still something that bothers me, that they didn't warn me that all the rehabilitation procedures + the operation could cost me NN amount of money. You can choose not to do them, but without them, you can't, unfortunately, I didn't complete the rehabilitation because I had to fly to another country. And there, with a masseur, I had to finish breaking up the lumps (they are normal after the operation, they will tell you about them). I also want to note that the rehabilitation period after the operation is actually twice as long as written in the advertising brochures.

On March 18, 2013, I gave birth to a son at the 20th maternity hospital. Everything went smoothly. However, I was sent home at 8 am after my mucus plug had released, as the doctor, Salikhova, said it was only the precursors of labor and my cervix was only dilated 1 cm. But by evening, the pains had intensified and became more frequent, so at 11 pm, my husband and I went back to the hospital.
This time, Dr. Khavantsov B.V. was on duty, he immediately sent me to the delivery room as I was 2-3 cm dilated. He then ruptured my membranes to speed up the process. He asked about my mindset for the delivery, I said I was very positive and calm, and he agreed that a positive attitude is crucial. He performed everything professionally. I wanted anesthesia, and Dr. Khavantsov explained its pros and cons. I was under anesthesia for the last 3 hours, so the delivery left only pleasant memories. The anesthesiologist, a man, was excellent, I don't know his last name, but he worked quickly. The relief after contractions without anesthesia was immense!
The midwife who delivered me was Badenkina N.A. I am incredibly grateful to her! She supported me, guided me on how to push and breathe. She is a wonderful, kind person and an excellent midwife. In short, my gratitude knows no bounds. The baby was born very easily, with just 3-4 pushes. I tore a little, but the cut was small, external, and healed quickly.
In the postpartum ward, I was placed in a single room, which was like a free VIP. The facilities were great, with a shower, toilet, and refrigerator. The doctor, Shilina I.L., also helped a lot after the delivery, explaining how to feed and express milk.
In conclusion, I want to thank all the staff of the 20th maternity hospital. To the expectant mothers, I want to say that childbirth is indeed associated with pain and emotions, so those who write that no one helped them, that they were shouted at, should initially set their mindset to positive. Then everything will be fine.

   g. A neighbor in the ward had an IV inserted so poorly that she now needs a surgeon's help, with a large lump and high fever on her arm.
   h. Doctors say, "If you don't like it, you can leave."

Ladies, there are many hospitals in Moscow, avoid 10 Roddom at all costs!

On May 27, 2011, I gave birth to a son! We arrived at the hospital with contractions every 5-7 minutes at 3:30 AM (my water broke in the morning of the 26th, and contractions started after a warm shower in the evening). There was no one else in the reception area, they did an ultrasound and examined me. The examining doctor was rude, but he was quickly put in his place. Then they gave me an enema and sent me to the delivery room. They did another ultrasound, attached a monitor, left me with "papaverin" suppositories that didn't help, and I asked for anesthesia, but it was too early as my dilation was small. An midwife stayed with me, teaching me how to breathe, talking to me, and giving me a ball that helped ease the contractions. Doctors kept coming in to examine me, around 11 AM they ruptured my membranes when I was completely exhausted and wanted to sleep. They decided to do an epidural, saying I could rest a bit. But as soon as they gave it to me, I relaxed and the process sped up. Within 10 minutes, I pushed once and gave birth! They didn't separate me from my baby, putting him on my stomach right away, and took us to the postpartum room together. They brought food almost immediately and checked that I went to the bathroom. I gave birth at 2:05 PM, and by 6 PM I was already walking around. Every day, doctors examined both me and the baby, teaching us how to care for him. The food was generally good, but there were products I couldn't eat as a breastfeeding mother. My relatives brought me everything, especially dairy products (which are necessary after birth to regulate digestion). Overall, I was very satisfied!

On May 27, 2011, I gave birth to a son! We arrived at the hospital with contractions every 5-7 minutes at 3:30 AM (my water broke in the morning of the 26th, and contractions started after a warm shower in the evening). There was no one else in the reception area, they did an ultrasound and examined me. The examining doctor was rude, but he was quickly put in his place. Then they gave me an enema and sent me to the delivery room. They did another ultrasound, attached a monitor, left me with "papaverin" suppositories that didn't help, and I asked for anesthesia, but it was too early as my dilation was small. An midwife stayed with me, teaching me how to breathe, talking to me, and giving me a ball that helped ease the contractions. Doctors kept coming in to examine me, around 11 AM they ruptured my membranes when I was completely exhausted and wanted to sleep. They decided to do an epidural, saying I could rest a bit. But as soon as they gave it to me, I relaxed and the process sped up. Within 10 minutes, I pushed once and gave birth! They didn't separate me from my baby, putting him on my stomach right away, and took us to the postpartum room together. They brought food almost immediately and checked that I went to the bathroom. I gave birth at 2:05 PM, and by 6 PM I was already walking around. Every day, doctors examined both me and the baby, teaching us how to care for him. The food was generally good, but there were products I couldn't eat as a breastfeeding mother. My relatives brought me everything, especially dairy products (which are necessary after birth to regulate digestion). Overall, I was very satisfied!

Citizens, I am in shock. All the enthusiastic reviews here are either from first-time mothers or those who have nothing to compare it to. I have something to compare it to. These were my third births, all previous ones were also free, but in different hospitals, and this was the worst choice I've made. I've already written about the bedding. A separate story about the "gratitude" that they started hinting at just 15 minutes after the birth, and every subsequent action towards me was accompanied by "hints". The question is, where do the funds from the birth certificate go, if at its nominal value of 6 thousand rubles, there's nothing in the hospital! I have a desire to draw the attention of the prosecutor's office and the Ministry of Health to this chaos. Further about the staff's work. No painkillers were prescribed (I had to prescribe them myself, ask the doctor, and then run after the nurse who was always busy to get the injection done). In three days, only one nurse, Elena Nikolaevna, remembered to treat the stitches. The pediatrician didn't even think it was necessary to come to the room and tell me about my child. I only saw the nurse (after a whole day!) who took the child, took it for an examination, and brought it back. When asked, "So, how's it going?", she replied, "Everything's fine." I'd like to ask again, "How's it going really?" A separate topic is the child whose clavicle was broken during birth, who cried constantly and didn't sleep, and only after the mother's insistence, more than a day later, the child was finally examined, the fracture was discovered, and a bandage was applied. The question is, where was the pediatrician immediately after the birth, why didn't he examine it immediately, the next morning, etc., and why does the mother have to run after everyone to make them do their job? What was particularly surprising was the presence of a child in the delivery room. A girl, the granddaughter of one of the employees, was running around the corridor, making noise, many mothers complained that they couldn't rest properly because of these cries. Excuse me, but is it allowed to have other children, besides newborns, in the delivery room? The cafeteria is something strange. I've never seen a cafeteria where it's clearly stated that meals are only served in the cafeteria. And here are the girls who, with great difficulty, come from the last births and eat standing up, instead of comfortably settling in their rooms and eating peacefully. And if the condition doesn't allow it, or the child is not sleeping at that moment, then the mother remains hungry. How awful! The food is terrible! It's just an insult to breastfeeding mothers. There's barely any meat in the diet, I only saw potatoes in the soup once in three days, instead of olive oil, there's olive margarine. Moreover, someone is constantly scolding, reprimanding you, you're always obliged to someone for something. In short, I signed a release form and left on the third day. Conclusion: This hospital is for those who are not first-time mothers, whose child is fine, and you know what to do, then the single room and staying with the child and the fact that no one bothers you (even with procedures) will please you very much.

Getting the results, we went back to the maternity hospital, where we were again met by "Olga Vladimirovna". With obvious displeasure, she accepted our tests, but still sharply rebuked us - there are no places, sit and wait. The news that we already had 41 weeks and it was time for us to give birth was unexpected and unpleasant for her, apparently, she could no longer refuse us for some medical reasons and left us waiting in the reception room for three hours. That's when we started thinking that free births in our time are almost like an anachronism, and no one will welcome us with open arms.
My wife was eventually accepted, but sent to "pathology" because her labor hadn't started. She mentioned a "cesarean", but was strictly refused - no indications. And then it began: she lay in the ward for half a day waiting for any doctor, but no one came. Then, the next day, a catheter was inserted into her cervix, supposedly "for gel application". It's impossible to ask for a pill or injection for pain relief - you're not allowed, endure it. The next two days, the doctors played hide and seek - they appeared rarely and mostly remained silent. At night, my wife's contractions started, instead of the labor ward, she was sent to the nurse who gave her sedatives and an injection. After the continuing contractions, she was finally sent to the labor ward, placed on a chair, and they left. A drip was put in and forgotten for three hours. After persistent cries, a nurse finally came, put on a CTG, and forgot again, resulting in a meter-long cardiogram and great surprise from the doctor who came later. My wife mentioned a "cesarean" again. The answer was the same - no indications. My wife, of course, fell asleep again right there on the chair from the tranquilizers. At noon, she was woken up by surprised doctors from the next shift - let's go for a "cesarean". For this, a separate thank you to the doctor who understood that it was dangerous to delay the birth any further. That is, after three days of doing nothing to help my wife give birth, they finally took her for surgery. Everything went well - the baby was taken out, shown, and taken away. My wife was sent to the ward.
And then the most interesting part began - in the large, beautiful wards, the "paying girls" lie happily, with their own doctor attached and a nurse running at the first call. My wife has the most ordinary "Soviet" ward, a duty doctor comes occasionally, and rude nurses. Want water? Go get it yourself - after surgery! Want extra food? Wait, we'll bring a 50-gram bottle in the evening. And so on, there's milk, there's no milk - feed as you can. My wife had her first birth, she asked to be taught how to feed. The answer was - if there are problems, come as you like. On the fifth day, she was discharged with great pleasure, and it seems they were waiting for new paying patients. We, Moscow residents, find this sad and unpleasant. We can only watch as guests from the former Soviet southern republics come to give birth to their numerous offspring, and the doctors and nurses are happy to "lick" them.

Hello dear girls, I myself have not given birth yet, it is only ahead of me in a couple of weeks, but I can say one thing for sure, that I would rather give birth in the wild forest than in the 18th maternity hospital. I was lying there on bed rest in August 2006, and now I am choosing a maternity hospital and stumbled upon this site and decided to share my impressions. I was admitted there with a diagnosis of premature placenta (fortunately, the diagnosis was not confirmed), let me start from the beginning: we arrived with my husband there early in the morning, because I understand that all the procedures in such places are done before lunch, and I really wanted to find out as soon as possible what was happening with my little one and if something was wrong, to start treatment as soon as possible (just a year before this pregnancy, I had a miscarriage and was very afraid that something would be wrong with this little one). We sat in the reception for quite a long time, despite the fact that there was no one else there, the girl accepting patients was very actively solving her personal problems on the phone and was not in the mood for us, but I, in general, did not expect to be welcomed with open arms, so I took it calmly. When the girl finally sorted out her personal life, she took me, not very well, rather indifferently, but it did not upset me, when she saw that I had passed all the tests in a private clinic, she asked me if I had a Moscow registration, although she had previously copied all my passport data (I am a native Muscovite), this rather amused me than upset me. They sent me to change and shave the bikini area, I handed over the clothes I came in to my husband, and then the medical staff quickly sent him away, and that's where it all started, the girl registering me started grumbling that, мол, the rich ones don't mind spending money on a private consultation, but we are here working for peanuts, I preferred to remain silent on this remark. An elderly woman came for me and took me to the procedure room, where she took some blood tests from me, saying that they don't trust my private doctor, and neither do I. After that, they took me to the ward, I didn't expect a five-star hotel, I understand that it's a state institution, but what I saw is indescribable, by education I am a lawyer and in the course of my work I had to visit places of detention (don't think anything bad, only for work), so I have seen detention cells cleaner than this ward, there was a clear handprint made with crumpled cookies on the wall above the bed that was assigned to me, and by all signs it was not one day or even one week old. Fortunately, my neighbors were very pleasant and we quickly found a common language, although both were significantly older than me. After I unpacked, I started waiting for the doctor, as they said he should come soon to call me to fill out something else. The doctor did not appear either after an hour or after two, but a woman who was not quite sober flew into the ward and shouted at us with our neighbors that if we smoke in the toilet, we will be thrown out of here with a kick in the ass, that everything here is sterile and such creatures as us are violating this sterility (I don't smoke at all because I used to be an athlete). The absence of the doctor worried me and I decided to go and ask where he was, I shouldn't have done that, they shouted at me so that I felt like a naughty child, as it turned out later, they simply forgot about me, but I took this fact with understanding, I am not the only one here, so what, it happens to everyone. It should be noted that my entire stay in this place was accompanied by wild screams of women in labor from the labor and pre-labor wards, which were located right next to us, and the door to the labor ward was always open, which eventually led to a nervous breakdown in one girl (about 15 years old), she was also lying on bed rest and happened to see the whole process with her own eyes, after which she started running around the corridor with wild screams: take the baby out of me, I don't want to give birth, they caught her quite agile nurses and put her in the ward with the words that if she doesn't shut up, she will go to a madhouse and even get a slap in the face. I, in general, understanding that I would not be able to have any procedures today, decided to go and take a shower, this was the biggest mistake of my life, the fact that the toilet and shower are for the entire floor did not bother me, but the picture that presented itself there bothered me very much. Mold was growing on the walls and curtains of the shower, which had not been cleaned for so long that it had already evolved to the point of inventing the wheel, this is not an exaggeration, the mold had been there for so long that some kind of beetles had already hatched in it, seeing this picture, the words of that woman who shouted at us earlier about sterility and so on came to mind. I returned to the ward and lay down to read, by the way, about food: dear girls, if you are picky about food, then take everything with you, I am not particularly picky about food, but I eat whatever is given to me. The time passed quite quickly and the first day was almost over, by evening we had become very friendly with our neighbors and it became easier to endure the screams of the poor girls from the labor ward, but even here we were waiting for a surprise, in the evening a woman came in and said that we were not allowed to talk loudly after 10 pm, otherwise we would be punished, we were very surprised by this, because we were not making any noise at all, we were just talking quietly among ourselves, but we decided not to argue and went to sleep. In the morning, we were woken up by the same woman who said that we had to leave the hospital by 10 am, we were very surprised by this, because we had not been given any treatment or procedures, we had only been lying there for a day, but we decided not to argue and left the hospital. In conclusion, I want to say that I understand that this is a state institution and there are not enough resources, but this is not an excuse for such a level of service, I would not recommend this maternity hospital to anyone, I would rather give birth in the wild forest than here.

My father, born in 1948, arrived at Moscow City Clinical Hospital No. 7 on his own two feet (weighing 74.8 kg) on May 22, 2012, and left in a coffin (exhausted) on July 18, 2012. The reason for his hospitalization was a peptic ulcer, with planned surgical treatment. He was admitted to the hospital on April 28, 2012, and discharged in satisfactory condition on May 16, 2012. A planned operation - gastric resection - was scheduled for May 23, 2012. The attending physician was Dr. Y.A. Bogdasarova, MD, PhD, Professor of the 2nd Department of Hospital Surgery, I.M. Sechenov First Moscow State Medical University.

Upon admission on May 22, my father's condition was assessed as satisfactory. On May 23, a gastric resection operation was performed by Dr. Bogdasarova (or her student, it's unclear). The operation was complicated by postoperative pancreatitis, caused by a bile duct injury, which is unacceptable. This injury was discovered a day later, by which time irreversible processes threatening his life had already begun. Treatment was initiated, and my father was repeatedly transferred between the intensive care unit and the surgical ward No. 12. From May 23 to July 18, 2012, he was fed through a feeding tube and drank very little due to his condition. He experienced constant pain. During his time out of the ICU, we provided round-the-clock care. In the ICU, his condition was neglected, leading to the development of decubitus ulcers on his sacrum and a burn on his back. Our complaints to the ICU staff were dismissed, as they claimed responsibility lay with the surgeons, who were not informed. We, along with my relatives visiting my father, had to notify the surgeons ourselves. The lack of coordination between the ICU staff and surgeons was evident. There were also numerous minor shortcomings in the surgical ward No. 12 that could jeopardize a patient's health. One such issue was the attitude of the on-call doctors during their shifts: they would either sleep (and couldn't be awakened) or arrive late after being called to attend to a patient in critical condition, citing heavy workload. Weekend rounds were often infrequent, giving the impression that the illness also had a day off.

We contacted the Moscow Department of Health. Their response stated that shortcomings in patient management had led to increased toxicity. The Chief Physician of Hospital No. 7 imposed disciplinary sanctions on the staff responsible for these shortcomings in providing medical care to my father.

My cousin was admitted to the hospital with acute chronic cholecystitis in the 2nd surgery department. He lived alone and upon admission said he had no close relatives. An operation was performed. They initially planned to do a laparoscopy but ended up doing an open surgery. The doctors were surprised when relatives arrived. After the operation, he felt well and his condition was improving. Then they inserted a dilator into his channel and that's when things started to go wrong. On the weekend, I visited him with a relative and was shocked by his condition. He was constantly vomiting, and IV drips were not helping. The on-call doctor didn't go into details, just looked at the vomit and changed the IV drip. They asked the nurses and orderlies to keep an eye on him overnight, of course, not for free. His ex-wife flew in from abroad. A strong, healthy man was wasting away before our eyes. The doctors said he needed to walk, but he couldn't get out of bed. He was vomiting and had severe diarrhea several times a day. His ex-wife begged the doctors, "Please get him on his feet. We'll reward you. Just cure him!" He was transferred to the ICU. They found two more ulcers in his duodenum. When talking to the doctors in the ICU, they said, "He was already very advanced, there's an inflammatory process. We're doing everything we can. There's no need to come here." In short, after 10 days in the ICU, he died. They found pneumonia. It turned out he was on a ventilator. Another operation was performed, but he didn't make it. I didn't have to talk to the surgeon; he was in the operation. I spoke with the head of the department. He explained everything in medical terms that we didn't understand. But how could a healthy 65-year-old man, who had never been sick, with excellent health, die after a routine operation from which patients are usually discharged after a week? The diagnosis was an abscess of the omental bursa. You can write anything you want in a diagnosis. My opinion, and not only mine, is that there is not enough care for patients now as there was in Soviet times. Everything depends on money. Maybe if we had paid immediately, everything would have been different? I don't know. God is the judge for all of us.

opinion_term: still didn't give me a definite diagnosis
english_translated:
At 16, I was in this hospital with appendicitis, and I was just shocked. I'll skip the part where they sent me to all the doctors because they couldn't figure out what was wrong with me. They still didn't give me a definite diagnosis and sent me for surgery: "Well, there's fluid in the pelvis, we need to do a laparoscopy to determine it exactly." (For those who don't know, that's when they make a small cross incision under the navel, insert a tube, inflate the abdomen with oxygen, and crawl around with a camera. Those who've had it done will agree it's not the most pleasant thing.)
The nice nurses came to prepare me. They undressed me, explained what they were going to do, put me on a gurney, and wheeled me away.
I was terrified: my first time in a hospital and straight to surgery. I was crying non-stop. During the laparoscopy, despite the anesthesia, it hurt so much from the oxygen pressing on my ribs and lungs that I couldn't even breathe. I told the anesthesiologist and begged, "Could you give me some pain medication?" He replied, "I don't owe you anything. Your mom and dad do. Endure."
There he was, standing by the table with a scared, crying 16-year-old kid, and he's being rude with a smug face.
Anyway, after some time, they diagnosed me with appendicitis and gave me full anesthesia.
It was Thursday night into Friday. All of Friday, I couldn't get up, but then they told me I had to walk. And on the weekend, I went to the bathroom for the first time without help.
Administrators, do you have a cleaner on weekends?!
There's excrement on the floor, the toilets aren't flushing because they're clogged, there's bloody paper and bandages in the trash bin, and the smell is just awful! Sanitation, my god!
I understand that there's construction going on and more people than usual in the wing, but then you need twice as many cleaners! This is A SURGERY WING! People are getting cut open here, and sanitation conditions are the most important thing!
So, I went to the bathroom, tensing all my muscles, making sure not to touch the toilet seat. I almost levitated over it.
In short, it was a mess, fear, and horror.

I understand that there's construction going on and more people than usual in the wing, but then you need twice as many cleaners! This is A SURGERY WING! People are getting cut open here, and sanitation conditions are the most important thing!
So, I went to the bathroom, tensing all my muscles, making sure not to touch the toilet seat. I almost levitated over it.
In short, it was a mess, fear, and horror.

I gave birth at the 67th maternity hospital in 2000, although I only needed a consultation, I had a cardiogram done in the 9th month, there was no time for consultation, and I was admitted to give birth. Some people say it's terrible, others say it's great, I experienced both. I was admitted two weeks in advance, I don't know the doctor, I saw her once a day before giving birth, and once after, but I had no strength to say anything. The treatment was limited to taking iron supplements and having my blood pressure measured, two interns were probably in charge, they showed care. I have the first negative blood group, blood was taken for antibodies two weeks in advance, but then they said the lab was overloaded, so they didn't take it again. I wasn't tortured, no heart examination was done, why I was admitted early is unclear. I didn't discuss the birth with the doctors, I gave birth for free. The birth itself was a nightmare, we both survived, probably thanks to the doctors, I'm very grateful to them. During the birth, there was a single, tight nuchal cord, the baby got stuck, the umbilical cord tightened, I couldn't feel the contractions, my lower abdomen, lower back, and the entire right side of my body seized up. The team that delivered me acted quickly, I tried to do everything they said, and they managed to pull the baby out without using forceps or causing oxygen deprivation. The first stage was over, then a trainee and someone from the internship team stitched me up, I said it hurts, but they said it can't be, they gave me anesthesia. They took me to the corridor, I felt really bad, a doctor passed by, noticed me, examined me, called the head of the maternity hospital, it turned out I had a uterine hemorrhage and a hematoma on the posterior wall, they sent me to the operating room, called the pros and saved me (I lay in the ICU for a bit) thanks to the doctors, although I still don't know their names. Now I'm waiting for my second, I went to the cardiologist for a consultation at the 67th, they asked me why I didn't have an echocardiogram done when I was with my first, it turns out I have a prolapse that I didn't know about and some other deviations. In general, I encountered both professionals and amateurs in turn, so where to give birth is up to you, there are amateurs everywhere, but the professionals at the 67th are good.

During the birth, there was a single, tight nuchal cord, the baby got stuck, the umbilical cord tightened, I couldn't feel the contractions, my lower abdomen, lower back, and the entire right side of my body seized up. The team that delivered me acted quickly, I tried to do everything they said, and they managed to pull the baby out without using forceps or causing oxygen deprivation. The first stage was over, then a trainee and someone from the internship team stitched me up, I said it hurts, but they said it can't be, they gave me anesthesia. They took me to the corridor, I felt really bad, a doctor passed by, noticed me, examined me, called the head of the maternity hospital, it turned out I had a uterine hemorrhage and a hematoma on the posterior wall, they sent me to the operating room, called the pros and saved me (I lay in the ICU for a bit) thanks to the doctors, although I still don't know their names. Discharged without being fully treated, still having a fever and without follow-up tests! I'm 27 years old, spent two weeks in the hospital with chronic purulent-obstructive bronchitis! They didn't do a control X-ray, didn't finish the physiotherapy, instead of the prescribed 10 times, I only got 5 magnet sessions and 6 inhalations, instead of 10. And it's all for nothing because my attending physician, Guumina Olga Lioniovna, if she can even be called a doctor, was negligent, rude, did rounds whenever she felt like it, sometimes not even looking at me. She completely ignored me, saying she'd come back later but never did. She didn't even look at my X-ray with pneumonia, which is what I was brought to the hospital for by ambulance. Plus, she said I only needed 2 antibiotics, but gave me 4-5 and kept changing them, so the treatment was practically useless. I was just like a rabbit to her. Guumina O.L. also increased my nebuhaler inhalation from 3 times a day to 4 times, even though my temperature was constantly rising after lunch, sometimes up to 38.5. I later found out that you shouldn't inhale with a nebuhaler when you have a fever. Before discharge (on the day of discharge), they took blood from my vein for a biochemical and clinical blood test. I asked if I should wait for the results, and they said, "If you need them so badly, come back tomorrow for the results." And today, we're discharging you!

Caution! Valentin Nikolaevich Borovkov. His professionalism is highly questionable. On August 23, 2014, my wife Svetlana underwent an osteosynthesis operation (a metal plate was installed). She had a closed comminuted fracture of the upper third of the tibia with displacement. She was discharged a week after the operation. My wife told me (she was conscious) how the operation went, including the use of an electric drill to drill holes in the bone for plate fixation. The drill fell on the floor and stopped working. They had to get another one. The instruments were not changed, after all, they are good as they are. During the removal of the sutures, the suture line opened up and was taped. They were discharged like that and told to apply green paint. Two weeks later, the tape was removed by themselves. A sore remained, which turned out to be necrosis. From the emergency room, where we were sent for further treatment, we were sent for a consultation to the 71st hospital where the construction was installed. The doctor said, "Let nature take its course." The question arises, why? Why first introduce infection in the form of golden staph, and then let nature take its course? My wife is very sociable, and every time we visited the emergency room, in line, we always met former patients of Valentin Nikolaevich Borovkov from the 1st traumatology department of the 71st hospital. In conversations with former patients of Valentin Nikolaevich Borovkov, it became clear that we are united by one thing - infection, that very notorious golden staph. Events continued to unfold, the plate became infected, the leg swelled up. A fistula opened up. People shied away from us, saying, "We'll have a hard time with you," when they found out that the plate was installed by Valentin Nikolaevich Borovkov from the 71st hospital (probably, Valentin Nikolaevich Borovkov is quite well-known among his colleagues). As a result, as of January 21, 2015, an Ilizarov apparatus is installed, the leg is 3 cm shorter, and disability is looming. Our case is not an isolated one. In 2012, Yelena Aleksandrovna Isaeva, born in 1973, had a more vivid experience with pictures. (http://mitin-deputat.livejournal.com/846.html) I want to appeal to the management of the 71st hospital. Please, put your house in order with both staff and hospital-acquired infection. There are already many disabled people, why increase their number? Sincerely, Vladimir.

On January 15-16, 2012, my wife and I accidentally spilled technical gasoline in the kitchen, which caught fire from a cigarette. I burned my legs up to my knees, and my wife burned her feet. We were admitted to the hospital. The night doctor treated our wounds and put us in separate wards. The next morning, the attending physician said that we needed a dressing change every two days. When I asked what we should do with ourselves, they simply told us to lie down and that was it. I asked if we could lie at home under our mother's supervision and come for dressing changes every two days. They said it didn't matter, but they wouldn't let us go, so I wrote a statement that I had no claims and did what I wanted. The hospital was dirty, unsanitary, the toilet was terrible, it was scary to go in, and it was impossible to call a nurse, they were always busy. So, I wrote a statement and went home. A familiar nurse did the dressing changes. A few days later, my wife's foot swelled up, we called an ambulance and went back to the hospital. The doctor smirked, "So, you're back!" My wife lay in the hospital for a few more days, calling me every two hours to say that everything hurt, no one was coming, the doctor said - dressings. It was difficult for her to go to the toilet, and a roommate took her on a wheelchair. Every time they passed the nurses' post, one of them would always reproach her, "They're taking you, your legs aren't broken." My wife would say, "You don't help, that's why the roommate is taking me." On Thursday, January 19, 2012, in the morning, my wife couldn't get out of bed, she took a chair as support and went to the duty room. I am 65 years old, 2 years ago I was diagnosed with chronic hip joint disease - coxarthrosis of 1-2 degree. Ismail Dibirov is an amazingly compassionate person and an excellent doctor.

At the beginning of this year, I started experiencing different kinds of pain, following his recommendation, I had an MRI of the lower spine, which revealed spinal osteochondrosis and a herniated disc. Therefore, on September 25, I was hospitalized in the neurology department No.2 of the Central Regional Hospital under the supervision of the head of the department - Victoria Sarikova, and the attending physician - Mikhail Smirnov. I received active treatment for both the spine and the hip joint. As a result, the severe leg pain subsided within 4 days. I would like to emphasize not only the high professionalism of the named doctors of both departments but also the entire medical staff - attentive, caring, and highly professional.
